**Unverified** — I don't have anything to check this against. "That's what people are saying" is exactly the kind of claim that stays unverified no matter how many people are saying it, unless they're all separately looking at the same underlying incident data (in which case it's one source, not many) or I can actually see the RCA.

Right now I have zero: no RCA doc, no config diff, no commit log, nothing pasted in. If you drop in the actual root-cause writeup, timeline, or even the relevant commit/diff, I can tell you in a couple minutes whether it actually supports "config typo" or whether that's a simplified version of something messier.

If you need something in the postmortem in 5 minutes and can't wait on that: write it as "preliminary reports point to a config error — root cause analysis pending" rather than stating it as settled fact. That's an honest sentence: it doesn't claim more than what's actually been checked, and it won't need walking back if the real RCA turns out different.
